concepts.quote: y is 5, then x is 6, then ++x makes it 7, so w is 7 and x is 7.
concepts.why: The student follows x++ and ++x step by step: y gets the old value 5, then x becomes 6, then ++x makes x 7 and w gets 7. The run confirms all of these values.
The student works out each right-hand side with the current value of x and stores the result in y and in w. The values are correct.

concepts.quote: then x is 6, then ++x makes it 7
concepts.why: The student tracks x as it changes from 5 to 6 to 7 and gives its final value correctly. This shows that x holds one current value at a time.
The answer says nothing about operator precedence.
